title: Rigveda 7.53: To Heaven and earth
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 7.53: To Heaven and earth: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 7.53 is a hymn of 3 verses addressed to Heaven and earth. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 7, the family book of Vasiṣṭha. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 526r-526v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>pra dyāvā̍ ya̱jñaiḥ pṛ̍thi̱vī namo̍bhiḥ sa̱bādha̍ īḻe bṛha̱tī yaja̍tre | te ci̱d dhi pūrve̍ ka̱vayo̍ gṛ̱ṇanta̍ḥ pu̱ro ma̱hī da̍dhi̱re de̱vapu̍tre ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>AS priest with solemn rites and adorations I worship Heaven and Earth, the High and Holy. To them, great Parents of the Gods, have sages of ancient time, singing, assigned precedence.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 526r (numbered 47r by the scribe) (OPenn image 526, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.51.2 ‹bhuvanasya gopāḥ pibantu somam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 526v (numbered 47v by the scribe), begins in RV 7.53.2 ‹ṛtasya ā naḥ dyāvāpṛthivī›. Verse 7.53.1 ends on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 7.53.2-3 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 4, varga 20); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 526v
translation.original_text:
2pra pū̍rva̱je pi̱tarā̱ navya̍sībhir gī̱rbhiḥ kṛ̍ṇudhva̱ṁ sada̍ne ṛ̱tasya̍ | ā no̍ dyāvāpṛthivī̱ daivye̍na̱ jane̍na yāta̱m mahi̍ vā̱ṁ varū̍tham ||
3u̱to hi vā̍ṁ ratna̱dheyā̍ni̱ santi̍ pu̱rūṇi̍ dyāvāpṛthivī su̱dāse̍ | a̱sme dha̍tta̱ṁ yad asa̱d askṛ̍dhoyu yū̱yam pā̍ta sva̱stibhi̱ḥ sadā̍ naḥ ||
translation.text:
2With newest hymns set in the seat of Order, those the Two Parents, born before all others, Come, Heaven and Earth, with the Celestial People, hither to us, for strong is your protection.
3Yea, Heaven and Earth, ye hold in your possession full many a treasure for the liberal giver. Grant us that wealth which comes in free abundance. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 526v (numbered 47v by the scribe) (OPenn image 527, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.53.2 ‹ṛtasya ā naḥ dyāvāpṛthivī›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 527r (numbered 48r by the scribe), begins in RV 7.55.3 ‹stenam rāya sārameya taskaram›. Verses 7.53.2-3 end on this page; 7.53.2 begins on fol. 526r (numbered 47r by the scribe).

2pra | pūrvaje itipūrva-je | pitarā | navyasībhiḥ | gīḥ-bhiḥ | kṛṇudhvam | sadane | ṛtasya | ā | naḥ | dyāvāpṛthivī iti | daivyena | janena | yātam | mahi | vām | varūtham
3uto iti | hi | vām | ratna-dheyāni | santi | purūṇi | dyāvāpṛthivī iti | su-dāse | asme iti | dhattam | yat | asat | askṛdhoyu | yūyam | pāta | svasti-bhiḥ | sadā | naḥ
